articles.title: Wu Shicun on why Beijing will not rule out Scarborough Shoal construction
articles.summary:
• Wu Shicun, founding president of China's National Institute for South China Sea Studies, argues that the Philippines' "assertive transparency" campaign since 2023 deliberately provokes Chinese responses (water cannon deployments, vessel interceptions) at Renai Jiao (Second Thomas Shoal), then packages these confrontations into viral videos to shape international perception of China as a bully.

• Wu says behind the Philippines' strategy lie domestic political goals — securing more budget and equipment for its coastguard from the Philippine Congress — alongside Western media support amplifying Manila's narrative.

• China has prioritized institutional rule-making, investing diplomatic capital in the Code of Conduct (COC) negotiations, ongoing since 2013, and the Declaration on Conduct of Parties (DOC) framework, whose working group recently held its 56th session.

• Wu acknowledges China was initially caught off guard by the Philippines' tactics during the 2023 Second Thomas Shoal standoff and later Sabina Shoal incidents, but has since adjusted its counter-strategy to proactively clarify and expose what it views as Manila's false narratives.

• Beijing is now shifting toward more proactive narrative construction in the South China Sea, with Wu characterizing this as a "profound paradigm shift" and describing it as the responsibility of a major power to counter disinformation.

articles.title: Zheng Yongnian on Trump, Venezuela and why China doesn’t want ‘a separate kitchen’
articles.summary:
• **Trump's strategic shift**: Zheng Yongnian identifies two core pillars of Trump's approach — consolidating US influence in the Western Hemisphere (the "Donroe Doctrine," an evolution of the Monroe Doctrine) and pursuing offshore balancing, moving away from deep post-WWII entanglement in Europe, the Middle East, and East Asia.

• **Strategic contraction is real this time**: Unlike the Obama era, when strategic contraction was discussed but never executed, Zheng argues Trump is action-oriented and capable of follow-through, making US withdrawal from existing global orders a credible scenario that will generate significant local turbulence.

• **Venezuela as a precedent, not an exception**: Zheng views Venezuela as part of a broader pattern, noting US right-wing think tanks are already discussing a tripartite partition of the world among major powers, paralleling Putin's long-standing efforts to carve out spheres of influence.

• **Ripple effects on smaller states**: European nations like Poland fear that a US-Russia compromise ceding Ukrainian territory would leave Ukraine as Russia's only target, and regional powers such as Turkey are asserting influence in their own neighborhoods (e.g., Turkic-speaking countries), signaling a fracturing of the existing order.

• **Global turbulence ahead**: Zheng predicts the defining trend of coming years will be structural instability regardless of whether the US retreats or advances, with big powers driving geopolitical shifts while smaller states scramble to adapt.

articles.title: Jeffrey Sachs says US sabre-rattling at China can become self-fulfilling prophecy of war
articles.summary:
Here is a summary of the article in bullet points:

- **Trade frictions will persist but remain bounded**: Sachs predicts that US-China trade tensions will continue to "wax and wane" after the tariff truce expires, but both sides will maintain limits on escalation because each holds chokeholds over the other (e.g., China's rare earth leverage prompted the US to back down from high tariffs).

- **The US initiated the trade war**: Sachs emphasizes that this is the US fighting China, not a mutual conflict, and notes that senior US officials appear "chastened," though Trump's unpredictability makes durable agreements unlikely.

- **China should diversify away from US and Western European markets**: Sachs advises China not to rely on the US as a growth market for exports, forecasting that rapid export growth will come from Africa, Southeast Asia, South Asia, West Asia, Central Asia, and Latin America rather than from the US or Western Europe.

- **Mutual economic interdependence provides a stabilizing check**: Both sides have strong reasons to achieve some cooperation because continued trade offers mutual gains, providing a measure of rationality that limits how far the competition can go.

articles.title: Liu Qian on Chinese innovation, the US rivalry and women holding up half the sky
articles.summary:
- **Liu Qian** is the founder of Wusawa Advisory, former managing director of The Economist Group in Greater China, and a leading advocate for gender equality and the sole Chinese representative in the core working group of the UN Women Leaders Network.

- Liu argues concerns about US-China trade tariffs are **overstated**: exports to the US represent only about **2.8 per cent of China's GDP** (exports overall fell from ~36% of GDP at peak to ~19% last year), meaning even a total loss of the US export market would impact only 2–3 per cent of China's economy.

- **ASEAN has overtaken the US as China's largest export destination**, and the export portfolio is diversifying rapidly — exports to **Brazil grew 23.3 per cent** last year and to **Africa by 25.9 per cent** in the first eight months of this year.

- Chinese exporters have shown **resilient and creative adaptation** — pivoting to new markets, products, and even packaging changes — and exports have generally held steady despite tariff pressures.

- Liu frames the US-China rivalry as extending well **beyond trade** into technology, ideology, and global collaboration, warning that continued unhealthy competition will harm both nations and the wider world; longer-term risks include impacts on unemployment, consumer confidence, business sentiment, and supply chain restructuring.

articles.title: Fuchsia Dunlop tells how she fell for China’s cuisine and names her perfect dish
articles.summary:
- Fuchsia Dunlop is a British author and chef widely regarded as the Western world's leading expert on Chinese cuisine, having written seven books specializing in China's diverse regional food cultures, particularly Sichuanese food.

- Her passion began in 1994 when she went to China as a British Council postgraduate student at Sichuan University, where she was captivated by the local food and convinced local restaurant owners to let her learn in their kitchens, eventually completing a chef's training course at the Sichuan Higher Institute of Cuisine.

- Upon returning to England, she noticed a complete lack of English-language Sichuan cookbooks and wrote her first book in 2001, unexpectedly launching a career dedicated to exploring Chinese food and culture.

- She notes that Sichuan food has become vastly more popular in the West since she started, and emphasizes that China's enormous size and culinary diversity mean there is always more to discover and write about.

- On mooncakes, Dunlop prefers savoury Shanghai minced pork mooncakes and various Yunnan varieties—including flaky pastry filled with Yunnan ham and larger Weishan-style cakes—over the more commonly known rich Cantonese lotus seed paste mooncakes.

articles.title: South Korea wants free ‘AI for All’. Is society ready?
articles.summary:
- **South Korea is launching an ambitious "AI for All" initiative** under President Lee Jae Myung's government, aiming to provide every citizen with free access to AI integrated into hospitals, schools, government offices, and daily life, positioning it as a permanent taxpayer-funded public utility by next year.

- **The government has committed significant funding**, with a 10 trillion won ($7.3 billion) AI budget for the current financial year plus an additional 250 billion won allocated through 2027. A beta version launching this month will offer free, unlimited-access chatbots and AI agents developed by SK Telecom, KT, and Kakao consortiums using state-of-the-art Nvidia B200 GPUs.

- **The push comes despite growing global warnings about AI risks**, including concerns from industry leaders like Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and AI pioneer Geoffrey Hinton about existential threats, autonomous weapons, mass unemployment, algorithmic bias, and deepfake-driven misinformation.

- **To manage these risks, Seoul is relying on regulatory and institutional safeguards**, including its landmark AI Basic Act (enforced since January) requiring human oversight, mandatory impact assessments, and synthetic content watermarking, alongside a state-funded AI Safety Institute acting as a technical watchdog guided by seven "AI Ethics Principles."

articles.title: Hong Kong’s historic vessels sail into the future
articles.summary:
• The Way Foong, a wooden motoryacht commissioned by HSBC and built in 1930 by the Hong Kong and Whampoa Dock Company, served the bank as a ferry, tugboat, and employee pleasure craft for over 7 decades before entering private ownership and later being acquired by the Hong Kong Historic Vessels Foundation (HKHVF).

• Java, a 1935-built 56-foot wooden vessel constructed by the same shipyard from Burmese teak with nearly 4.5cm-thick deck planks, served in Hong Kong's government fleet as Marine 1 for VIP transport, anti-piracy patrols, and buoy operations, earning a reputation as "almost unsinkable."

• The HKHVF, founded in 2024, now owns and maintains five historic vessels; its founders launched the effort after one of them discovered Java moored in Tai Tam Harbour in the early 2000s and eventually began a broader mission to preserve Hong Kong's maritime heritage.

• A years-long search by the foundation's historians has identified nine pre-1950s boats built in Hong Kong — some now in the HKHVF collection, others privately owned, and one, Mon Lei, whose whereabouts remain unknown.

articles.title: Talk is growing of a Tesla-SpaceX merger. Will geopolitics throw a spanner in the works?
articles.summary:
- Tesla's Gigafactory in Shanghai is a major export hub, delivering 93,579 vehicles in July alone, with a record 7,738 Teslas shipped on a single vessel; more than half of the factory's 2024 output is exported overseas, making it highly efficient but geopolitically vulnerable.

- Elon Musk faces a balancing act as his EV empire relies heavily on China's supply chain while his SpaceX company serves as a core Pentagon national-security contractor, creating potential conflicts between US and Chinese interests.

- Growing speculation surrounds a possible Tesla-SpaceX merger, driven by deepening technology overlap in AI, robotics, and other areas; while Musk has not publicly confirmed or denied the idea, the merger could intensify national-security scrutiny from Washington given SpaceX's ties to the US government.

- Industry analysts note that Tesla and SpaceX are increasingly becoming mutual suppliers—Tesla providing solar panels, batteries, and components for SpaceX, while SpaceX supplies its Grok AI model and Starlink connectivity for Tesla products—making a formal closer integration increasingly plausible but geopolitically complex.

articles.title: Antwerp: a well-seasoned melting pot of Rubens, diamonds and Belgium’s only Chinatown
articles.summary:
• Antwerp (population 568,000), located 40 minutes north of Brussels by train, is renowned for its Flemish cultural heritage, including masterworks by Baroque painter Peter Paul Rubens, a Royal Museum of Fine Arts featuring artists from Jan van Eyck to René Magritte, and Renaissance-era guild-houses and merchant mansions from its golden age as the world's leading port in the early 16th century.

• The city is a diverse cultural melting pot shaped by successive waves of immigration: Jewish refugees expelled from Spain in the late 15th century who later established a global diamond trade hub; settlers from the Maghreb and Central Africa during Belgium's colonial era; post-WWII immigrants from Hong Kong and mainland China who created Belgium's only official Chinatown; and recent refugees from Afghanistan, Syria, Iraq, Somalia, and Ukraine.

• Antwerp's late-19th-century Central Station, often called a "railway cathedral" with its dome, marble staircase, frescoes, and stained-glass windows, frequently wins awards as the "World's Most Beautiful Station." Immediately outside its gates, a pagoda gate marking Chinatown sits adjacent to an Orthodox Jewish community on Pelikaanstraat.

• Approximately 120 diamond and gold jewellery boutiques operate within a single square mile around the diamond district, largely run by a tight-knit Jewish community whose lingua franca remains Yiddish, with merchants like goldsmith Yosef Degan specializing in buying, melting, and reworking old gold into unique designs.

articles.title: Temu took the world by storm – but has the shopping app lost its thunder?
articles.summary:
- **Temu's explosive growth**: In February 2023, budget shopping app Temu gained massive visibility through a $14 million Super Bowl ad campaign ("Shop like a billionaire"), causing app downloads to jump 45% overnight. The platform rapidly expanded globally, bringing Chinese-style ultra-low-price e-commerce to markets worldwide.

- **Foundational business model**: Temu's ultra-low prices were built on two pillars: leveraging parent company PDD Holdings' mature Chinese supply chain — refined through years of operating Pinduoduo — and a distribution strategy that circumvented hefty import tariffs via direct shipping from Chinese warehouses to global consumers.

- **China's manufacturing ecosystem as key advantage**: Temu tapped into China's deeply concentrated manufacturing clusters (e.g., Dongguan for electronics/toys, Foshan for furniture), where factories, suppliers, and logistics networks enable unmatched production scale and cost efficiency.

- **Growing regulatory headwinds**: Three years on, Temu's business proposition is under pressure as rising global regulation and customs barriers erode the tariff-avoidance and low-cost shipping advantages that made its pricing model viable.

articles.title: Thailand has had enough of foreign tourists behaving badly
articles.summary:
- Tourism contributes roughly one-fifth of Thailand's economy, yet international visitor numbers have failed to recover to the pre-pandemic peak of nearly 40 million in 2019; last year's total of 32.9 million fell short despite a 2024 visa-free scheme, and the Tourism Authority of Thailand has trimmed its 2026 forecast to 30–34 million visitors.

- The Covid-19 pandemic permanently shifted tourism trends in Thailand, replacing large bus-tour groups (especially from China) with "free, independent tourists" (FITs), devastating traditional businesses like the Samut Prakan Crocodile Farm that relied on mass group tours.

- Geopolitical conflicts — the US-Israel war on Iran and Russia's ongoing war with Ukraine — are driving up oil prices and international airfares to Southeast Asia, further suppressing travel demand.

- A persistently strong Thai baht has made the country comparatively expensive, pushing budget-conscious travelers toward cheaper alternatives like Vietnam and Malaysia.

- Beyond money and geopolitics, the article indicates that years of increasingly bad behavior by foreign tourists have eroded Thailand's patience and contributed to the downturn in visitor appeal.

articles.title: Going ‘car-lite’: why more Singaporeans are quitting driving
articles.summary:
- **Soaring car ownership costs are driving Singaporeans to abandon cars**: COE prices have risen from S$10,000 in 2006 to over S$112,000 for renewal, alongside increases in road tax, fuel, maintenance, insurance, and ERP congestion charges, prompting many to quit driving entirely.

- **Private car numbers hit a multi-year low**: As of July, Singapore had 516,237 privately owned cars—the lowest since 2019—while rental, ride-hailing, and corporate cars have grown as a share of total vehicles on the road.

- **Singapore is pursuing a "car-lite" policy**: The government's "Move Lite" campaign, launched in 2022, encourages walking, cycling, and public transport use, shifting its messaging from highlighting public transport benefits to spotlighting the downsides of driving.

- **ERP congestion charging continues to expand**: Electronic road pricing returned to Singapore's Orchard Road shopping district in early August 2024, the first reinstatement since the pandemic, as part of broader road usage management.

- **Balancing competing transport needs**: The Land Transport Authority frames its strategy around investing in public transport and active mobility infrastructure while managing vehicle ownership and road usage to efficiently allocate Singapore's limited land resources.

articles.title: From kitchen waste to sky-high costs: inside Hong Kong’s quest for green jet fuel
articles.summary:
- **Gutter oil has transformed from a food safety issue into a valuable feedstock** for producing sustainable aviation fuel (SAF), with its cost now exceeding that of conventional fuel; SAF can reduce life-cycle carbon emissions by up to 80% and is a "drop-in" substitute requiring no aircraft engine modifications.

- **Hong Kong's government has set a revised 2030 SAF target of 1–3%** of all fuel used by departing flights (up from an initial 1–2%), which industry analysts at S&P Global consider a cautious but achievable goal; the city also aims to develop a competitive SAF value chain in the Greater Bay Area.

- **Cost and policy clarity remain the central challenges**, as airlines, producers, and investors await clear guidance on who will bear the expense; Cathay Pacific's CEO stressed that a well-designed policy is needed to connect producer confidence, airline affordability, and investment certainty.

- **Hong Kong is positioned as a potential trial site for mainland China's SAF rollout**, given its status as one of the world's busiest airports (61 million passenger trips and 5.07 million tonnes of cargo in 2023) and its role as a dominant Asian aviation hub alongside Singapore.

commentary:
# "微笑之国"的微笑还能维持多久？——泰国旅游业衰落的政治经济学审视

**一、现象描述**

泰国旅游业疫情后未能恢复至2019年近4000万人次的峰值，游客数量持续下滑，外国游客失当行为激化社会矛盾，旅游经济结构性脆弱日益暴露。

**二、政治经济学定位**

泰国旅游业本质上是一种高度依赖外部需求的服务商品出口产业。旅游业约占泰国经济总量的五分之一，从普吉岛的五星级度假村到芭提雅的按摩院，资本的运动逻辑始终围绕着将泰国的自然资源、气候条件和人力资源转化为可供国际消费者购买的商品。这一体系的根基在于国际资本的流动方向和全球消费者的购买力分布，而非泰国自身的生产性积累。

正如马克思所揭示的，"资本主义生产不仅是商品的生产，它实质上是剩余价值的生产"（《资本论》第一卷·第五章）。泰国旅游业的全部秘密在于：外国资本——无论是国际航空集团、跨国酒店连锁、OTA平台还是入境旅行社——控制着价值链的高端环节，攫取着远超其投入的剩余价值；而泰方参与者，尤其是基层劳动者，则被压缩在低附加值的劳动密集型岗位上。鳄鱼农场创始人查隆所经历的从外国旅行团到"自由行散客"的转变，表面上是消费偏好的变迁，实质上是国际旅游资本重组其全球供应链的结果——大规模团队旅游的组织形式被更灵活、利润率更高的散客经济所替代，但利润向平台资本集中的趋势并未改变。

**三、深层结构分析**

泰国旅游业的组织形式遵循资本主义分工深化的逻辑。马克思指出，"工场手工业分工通过手工业活动的分解、劳动工具的专门化，造成了社会生产过程的质的划分和量的比例"（《资本论》第一卷·第十一至十三章）。旅游业正是这一过程的当代延伸：从交通运输、住宿、餐饮、娱乐到零售，每一个环节被精细拆解并纳入跨国资本主导的全球服务链条。泰国被锁定在生产链的低端——提供土地、劳动力和自然资源，而品牌、技术、客源分配和金融结算则掌握在外部资本手中。这种结构性从属地位使泰国旅游业在每一次外部冲击面前都极度脆弱：SARS、禽流感、2007-08年金融危机、新冠疫情，无一例外。

更为根本的是，旅游业的劳动组织形式对劳动者造成了深刻的损害。正如马克思所言，分工"损害了工人的整个劳动能力，使工人畸形发展"。大量旅游从业者被禁锢在按摩师、服务员、司机、导游等高度专门化的岗位上，缺乏转行能力和议价能力。疫情期间的封锁使这一脆弱性暴露无遗——当资本流动中断时，这些劳动者的生存随即陷入困境。

**四、阶级与利益分析**

旅游业繁荣的受益者远非泰国全体民众。国际航空资本、跨国酒店集团、数字平台资本和入境旅行社构成的垄断联盟，控制着从客源分配到利润分配的全部环节。泰国本土的中大型旅游企业主虽能分得部分利润，但同样受到外部资本的制约。泰国社会评论家沃拉奈所言"泰国人是务实的，我们喜欢旅游带来的钱"，恰恰点明了资本逻辑对社会共识的收编——基层劳动者以廉价劳动力的身份被纳入这一体系，却难以分享资本增殖的果实。

游客失当行为之所以引发强烈的民族主义反弹，正是因为底层民众在承受旅游业全部的负外部性——物价上涨、资源消耗、文化侵蚀、治安恶化——的同时，获得的经济回报却极为有限。愤怒指向的是"不守规矩的外国游客"，但结构性矛盾的根源在于：泰国被嵌入全球资本主义体系后，其经济自主性丧失，劳动力被商品化为国际消费的供给方。

**五、主流叙事批判**

泰国政府和主流媒体的叙事框架将问题归结为"游客素质下降"和"竞争国家的廉价替代"，推出签证免签等促销措施试图挽救客流量。这完全是治标不治本。将旅游业下滑归咎于"越南和马来西亚更便宜"，遮蔽了问题的实质：在全球资本自由流动的体制下，劳动力价格被压至最低的国家才能赢得竞争——这是一场无底线的向下竞赛。而将外国游客塑造为"不文明的冒犯者"，则将阶级矛盾转化为民族矛盾，将结构性剥削的问题置换为文化尊重的问题。正如查隆的鳄鱼农场曾为迎合中国旅行团建造的城堡式外墙，如今"斑驳褪色"——泰国为迎合国际资本需求而修建的一切基础设施，在资本转移后即沦为废墟。

**六、解放前景**

泰国旅游业的困境绝非短期周期性波动，而是依赖型资本主义结构性矛盾的必然体现。真正的出路不在于吸引更多游客或维持更低廉的价格，而在于重新夺回对生产资料和分配环节的控制权。首先，必须打破跨国资本对旅游价值链的垄断性控制，推动酒店、交通和旅行社的本土化和合作社化。其次，经济结构必须多元化，将资源从服务出口导向的旅游业转向具有自主技术能力的生产性部门。正如马克思揭示的，"较多的工人在同一时间、同一空间……在同一资本家的指挥下工作，这在历史上和逻辑上都是资本主义生产的起点"——当劳动者不再处于"同一资本家的指挥下"，而是以劳动者联合体的形式组织生产，剩余价值才可能真正留在本国、留给劳动者。泰国"微笑之国"的微笑，只有当劳动者的微笑不再被资本收编为商品时，才可能是真实的。
